correctness.rationale:
For a two-dimensional dihedral irreducible, the rotation projectors have off-diagonal phase \(cq^j\), with \(q=\zeta^{2k}\) and \(m=\operatorname{ord}(q)\). When \(m>2\), cycle averages of the rotation and reflection orbits span both diagonal directions exactly when \(|a|
e|b|\), and the first Fourier coefficients isolate \(E_{12}\) and \(E_{21}\) exactly when \(a\overline b
e0\); the unwanted coefficient vanishes because \(\sum q^{2j}=0\). When \(m=2\), the two off-diagonal Hermitian directions are independent exactly when \((a\overline b)^2-(\overline a b)^2
e0\), equivalently \(\operatorname{Im}((a\overline b)^2)
e0\). No two-dimensional irrep has \(m=1\). Hence the two stated criteria are necessary and sufficient, and the explicit vectors work. The one-dimensional irreducibles are immediate. The finite replay through \(n=80\) was inspected only as corroboration; the universal conclusion is discharged by the root-of-unity calculation.

originality.rationale: Fresh comparison found general maximal-spanning criteria, affine-group matrix-recovery results, nilpotent/p-group phase-retrieval results, and dihedral full-spark/Haar results, but no materially inspected theorem stating that every finite-dihedral irreducible does matrix recovery or giving the exact \(m>2\) versus \(m=2\) generator criterion. The 2025 Cheng article is the strongest priority risk: its title and indexing directly concern irreducible finite-group phase retrieval and maximal spanning vectors. Open and public full-text routes did not provide the paper, and the authorized institutional retrieval returned a different 2023 article despite the requested DOI, so that route was not retried or bypassed. Under the owner rule this inaccessible plausible source is recorded as a substantial residual risk rather than converted into a scientific failure.
